profile.reading:
CloudHQ LC5 sits at 21615 Lockridge Road, Ashburn, Virginia, one of fourteen numbered buildings on CloudHQ's LC Campus, which the company's own current campus page places directly off Loudoun County Parkway "in the heart of Ashburn," describing the site as sitting amid "the densest concentration of fiber in the world." CloudHQ states the full LC Campus totals roughly 8.5 million square feet and 1,256 megawatts of total critical IT load across its fourteen data centers, with 756 megawatts currently available; this is a campus-wide total that CloudHQ does not break out by individual building, and no third-party aggregator figure specific to LC5 was found either. CloudHQ was founded in 2016 by Hossein Fateh, who also founded QTS Realty Trust and, per CloudHQ's own materials, was the first person in the United States to obtain an IRS ruling allowing data center income to qualify for real estate investment trust tax treatment. CloudHQ is privately held through the Fateh Family Office, with regional headquarters in Washington DC, London, and Singapore, and states a company-wide net-zero emissions target by 2040, along with generator fuel supplied by HVO biodiesel "wherever it is reliably available" and a stated goal of net biodiversity gain on all new campuses. CloudHQ markets a "campus within a campus" concept at LC, allowing customers to take multiple LC-numbered buildings as one contiguous deployment. CloudHQ does not name a power utility for the LC Campus on its current site; Dominion Energy is the dominant electric utility across Loudoun County as a matter of public record.

Loudoun County's Ashburn corridor is the largest concentration of data center capacity in the world, hosting dozens of competing hyperscale and colocation operators, including Amazon Web Services, Digital Realty, NTT, Vantage, and Centersquare/Csquare facilities, within a few miles of CloudHQ's LC Campus. CloudHQ's global portfolio spans 23 campuses and more than 30 million square feet across six countries, with more than 1,380 megawatts of critical IT load already contracted company-wide, and trade press has separately reported CloudHQ planning a 4-million-square-foot expansion campus in Ashburn beyond the LC Campus's existing footprint.

reading.body:
CloudHQ LC5 is one of fourteen buildings on the LC Campus in Ashburn, Virginia, a 8.5 million square foot site with 1,256 megawatts of total critical IT load and 756 megawatts currently available across all fourteen facilities combined. The operator does not publish capacity figures specific to LC5, so the building's individual size and power draw cannot be determined from available sources. The LC Campus sits directly in Ashburn's corridor, which hosts dozens of competing hyperscale and colocation operators including AWS, Digital Realty, NTT, Vantage, and Centersquare within a few miles.

At 1,256 megawatts across 8.5 million square feet for the full fourteen-building campus, the average density is roughly 148 watts per square foot of IT load. If LC5 represents an equal share of that campus capacity, it would hold approximately 90 megawatts of total critical IT load, which at the assumption of 40 kilowatts per rack would be roughly 2,250 racks. This is an estimate only, based on an assumption of equal distribution across all fourteen buildings, and does not reflect any published figure for LC5 itself.

The LC Campus ranks 24th among the 23 Virginia facilities with published megawatt figures on this site, meaning only the full campus total has entered public capacity tracking. Virginia hosts 330 mapped data center facilities overall, of which only 23 publish power capacity, for a statewide total of 1,375 megawatts. CloudHQ does not name a specific power utility for the LC Campus, though Dominion Energy is the dominant electric utility across Loudoun County.
